Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Following up with two things we need to converge so we can lock committed capacity by EOM for HL-2397:

1) Finalized monthly token/throughput profile (attached "initial_capacity_model.xlsx"). Please confirm the three-month peak and 12-month baseline numbers in the model — the staging pool assumptions are calling for a 2x peak headroom for canary rollouts.

2) OEM quote alignment: we need Quanta's formal quote (unit pricing + lead time) and Nebula cloud's burst/priority capacity confirmation so we can build the mixed procurement plan we discussed.

I've attached the SOW draft (Helium_SOW_v1.pdf) so you have the high-level acceptance criteria. Can we get the Quanta quote and Nebula capacity note by Tuesday (05/07)? If that timeline is tight, please flag which items will slip.

Quick ask: please confirm whether Helium wants a single vendor reserved pool or a split reserved (OEM) + cloud burst topology. Our default recommendation is a 70/30 split for cost predictability but we'll adapt to your preference.

Thanks — looping Karthik, Ben, and Monica for procurement and vendor coordination.

Best,
Lauren Bishop

Thanks, got the materials. Quick answers:

- We validated the baseline and three-month peak in the spreadsheet; the team expects higher burst activity in month 2 due to a planned marketing push. I added a comment in the sheet where that shows up.

- Helium prefers a split topology (reserved OEM + cloud bursts) but we'd like the reserved portion to cover 60–70% of steady-state. We're OK with a 70/30 split if the lead times and price delta to Nebula make sense.

- Quanta: we reached out to them last week; they said they could provide a formal quote but their standard lead time for the SKUs we discussed is 14–18 weeks. We'll share the contact if you need to escalate.

Hi all —

Quick vendor note from procurement side. I spoke with Quanta and they provided a preliminary PDF quote (attached quanta_quote_0428.pdf). Key items:

- Lead time: quoted 14 weeks from signed PO for the base SKU, 18 weeks for the denser variant.
- Minimum tranche: 32 units per shipment; they can do two tranches with six weeks between them to accelerate initial availability.
- Pricing: ~3% discount if Helium signs a 12-month reserved commitment; better pricing tiers available for higher commits.

Proposal for Helium HL-2397:
- Stage 1 (weeks 0–12): Nebula bursts to cover marketing spike + a 32-unit tranche from Quanta to start canaries.
- Stage 2 (weeks 12–20): Second Quanta tranche to complete reserved pool to 70% steady-state.

If Quanta's 14-week lead time is firm we should plan the PO signature this week to hit the timeline. Ben will run the PO process if Helium confirms the split.

Team —

Thanks Ben and Emily. A few procurement constraints and requests from our side before we execute:

1) Payment & delivery terms: Quanta's quoted 14–18 weeks is acceptable but we need to confirm the Incoterms and whether Quanta can split invoices per tranche. Helium legal has to sign standard Purchase Terms; please flag if Quanta needs SLA exceptions.

2) Lead-time mitigation: If Helium wants earlier capacity we can frontload Nebula burst credits for the first 8–12 weeks. However, Nebula preemption and throttling behavior must be acceptable for the canary. Emily — can you confirm tolerance?

3) Customs & staging: Quanta ships from Singapore; expect 7–12 days for customs/port clearance after factory ship date. We should build a 2-week buffer into the go-live plan for unexpected clearance delays.

4) Rollout policy: Recommend a canary window of 72 hours with KV-cache warmup and a fallback route to Nebula for sustained latency spikes. Monica, can you prepare the deployment rollout checklist?

If everyone agrees, I'll prepare the procurement checklist and a two-tranche PO template for Ben to use.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Infrastructure Ops, Redwood Inference
